input.quote: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 binds only Customer, is an outright no-hire ("hire, or employ"), covers every Vendor employee rather than personnel involved in the Services, runs 24 months, and negates any general-advertising or unsolicited-application carve-out. It fails the fallback on every material term and is walk-away territory. At the locked preferred level no non-solicit may bind Customer, so we flip the prohibitory operator ("shall not" to "may") and strike the 24-month tail, leaving no restriction, residual duration, or negative implication. The fallback's mutuality, service-personnel scope, 12-month involvement period and carve-outs are deliberately not added, as preferred and fallback are separate bargains; the fallback is offered in the margin comment only. The edit also aligns the operative text with Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no no-hire commitment.

ops.oldText: Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
ops.newText: Customer may solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee, regardless of how the employee applies.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have flipped the prohibition in 12.4 so no non-solicit or no-hire binds Customer and struck the 24-month tail, consistent with Section 12.3 where Vendor acknowledges we have made no no-hire commitment. If Vendor needs protection, we can discuss a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months after their involvement ends, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches and no no-hire element.
proposal.summary: Remove the one-way 24-month no-hire binding Customer (§12.4)
